lines.text: Hi! This is a MyCast demo, and today we are on the Acropolis in Athens.
The rock above the city where the Parthenon stands. Where did it come from?
It was built in the fifth century BC as a thanksgiving for the Greek victory over the Persian invaders. Construction started in 447 BC.
How long did the work take?
The temple itself was finished in 438 BC, and the sculptures and decoration went on until 432. The architects were Iktinos and Callicrates.
And inside stood a huge statue of Athena by Phidias, right?
Right. Interestingly, the temple was also a treasury. For a time it held the funds of the Delian League.
So it was a temple and a bank at once. But today the Parthenon has no roof. What happened?
It had a stormy history. At the end of the sixth century AD it became a Christian church, and after the Ottoman conquest, a mosque.
In 1687, during the Venetian siege of the Acropolis, a bomb hit the Parthenon, which the Ottomans used to store gunpowder. The explosion wrecked much of the building.
What about the sculptures that survived?
In the early nineteenth century Lord Elgin took many of them to England. People still argue about where they belong.
And since 1975 Greece has run large restoration projects there.
So when you look at the Parthenon, you see twenty-five centuries of history in one stone.
That was a MyCast demo episode. You can build your own podcast at mycast.pro.
